projects.title: Experiments
projects.subtitle: Design and run your algorithm studies.

empty.title: Design your first experiment
empty.body: An experiment is your study: a set of simulated users (bots) that browse a platform so you can observe what its algorithm surfaces to each one. Create one and we'll walk you through the setup.

composer.subtitle: The ordered steps this run performs, top to bottom.
composer.empty: No jobs yet. Add the first step below.
composer.name: Label
composer.addError: Couldn't add the job. Please try again.
composer.degradedNotice: Some jobs finished but degraded — their data was not written, or a filter this bot requested could not be applied. (A video picked at random is normal for a control bot; it is a problem only when a treatment was requested and did not take effect.) Check those jobs before using this run's data.
composer.tallyHint: Counted from the jobs below. The run's own status above is what the runner reported.
composer.unknownHint: The API reported a status this app does not recognise. Not a success — check the job.
composer.partialTallyHint: This page loaded the first jobs of the run only. The alarm figures above come from the API’s count over the whole run; the tally beside them counts the jobs on screen.

behaviours.title: Behaviours
behaviours.subtitle: The type-specific settings for this job (name → value).
behaviours.empty: No behaviours yet. Add the settings this job needs below.
behaviours.name: Setting

profile.title: Profile
profile.subtitle: Who this bot is when it browses: its location, cookie consent, how it uses the platform, and the weights the YouTube decision function reads. Shared by every run of this bot.
profile.none: This bot has no configuration, so it has no profile to edit. Pick one under Library when you set the bot up.
profile.defaultsHint: Not set yet: {{names}}. The experiment designer gives every bot these.
profile.decisionHint: Numbers passed to the decision function when it picks what this bot watches. Their range is defined by that service.

hint.cookie: How the bot answers cookie banners

error.duplicate: Already set. Edit the existing row instead.
error.cookieKey: Needs an "accept_all" key, e.g. {"accept_all": true}. The runner ignores anything else.
error.generic: The profile could not be saved.

treatment.title: Treatment
treatment.subtitle: What this bot searches for and which results it picks. The runner scores every result by the bot's political position against the outlet's, so these numbers are the experiment's manipulation.
treatment.shared: Shared by {{count}} bots: changes apply to all of them
treatment.multiple: This configuration has {{count}} parameter rows. The runner uses the first one (#{{id}}), which is the one shown here.
treatment.noneBody: No treatment set. The runner has no parameters to select results with, so this bot's choices are not controlled.

pi.label: Political position
pi.hint: −1 left … 0 centre … 1 right. Results from outlets near this position score higher.

psi.label: Persuadability
psi.hint: 0 to 1: how far this bot can be moved by what it sees. Also sent to the YouTube decision function.

kappa.label: Persuadable
kappa.hint: 0, 1 or 2: whether this bot can be persuaded at all (0 = not). Also sent to the YouTube decision function.

tau.label: Distance cost
tau.hint: How strongly ideological distance to an outlet lowers its score. 0 = indifferent.

alpha.label: Known-outlet bonus
alpha.hint: Extra score for results from an outlet in the list below.

beta.label: Rank penalty
beta.hint: Score lost per position down the result list. 0 = rank does not matter.

terms.title: Search terms
terms.hint: What the bot may search for, each with a political position.

outlets.title: Media outlets
outlets.hint: Outlets the bot knows, each with a political position. A result counts as this outlet when its address is on this domain.
outlets.savedAs: Saved as {{domain}}, the form the runner matches

csv.bad: Not imported, could not read line(s) {{lines}}.

error.kappa: Must be a whole number, 0 or more.
error.generic: The treatment could not be saved.

bot.title: Add your first bot
bot.body: A bot is a simulated user. We'll create one with sensible defaults — open Advanced to set its browser identity, connection and behavior.
bot.name: Bot name

runs.title: Plan the runs
runs.body: Runs are scheduled per bot. Each run is one timed session your bot performs — you build its job sequence and behaviours on the bot's page.
runs.later: When you finish, we'll take you straight to your bot's page so you can schedule its first run.

review.title: Review & create
review.body: Here's what we'll create. You can refine every part afterwards.

badge.treatmentLostHint: This bot was configured to be treated but produced control-arm data — this session carries no treatment signal, even though the job finished.
badge.degradedHint: Part of the treatment did not apply.
badge.noVerdictHint: No decision verdict was recorded for this job. Not the same as a clean one — it predates the change, or the runner has not been redeployed.

tooltip.selectionMode: Chosen by: {{mode}} (description only, not a verdict)

report.title: Decision report
report.noVerdict: This job does not call the decision function, so there is no verdict to show.
report.noVerdictLambda: No verdict was recorded for this job. That is not a clean result — the job predates the change, or the runner writing it has not been redeployed. The archived payload may still hold the answer.
report.treatmentLost: Treatment lost — this bot was configured to be treated and produced control-arm data.
report.degraded: Degraded — a requested filter did not apply.
report.clean: No degradation reported for this decision.
report.selectionModeHint: a description of how the video was picked, not a verdict; “random” is correct for a control bot

raw.error: The raw payload could not be read. That says nothing about whether the treatment applied — only that this archive could not be reached.

alarm.jobs: Treatment lost in {{count}} job(s) of this run.
alarm.experiment: Treatment lost in {{count}} run(s) in this window.
alarm.hint: Those sessions produced control-arm data although a treatment was configured, so their observations carry no treatment signal.
alarm.runsUnlisted: Treatment lost in {{runs}} run(s) of this bot in the last 24 h — not all of them are accounted for in the list below.

statusFilter.badHint: Failed or degraded — the two states a human should look at. Legacy spellings such as "failed" are included; the API expands them.
statusFilter.warningHint: Completed, but degraded: something the experiment cares about did not happen.
statusFilter.failureHint: Did not complete. Includes rows recorded with the legacy spelling "failed".
statusFilter.successHint: Completed with nothing reported as degraded.

empty.title: Nothing matches this filter
empty.body: That is a statement about the filter, not about the bot: other runs exist, they are just in other states.

health.title: Health

window.7dHint: Runs from the last 7 days (168 h).
window.allHint: The endpoint's maximum window: the last 30 days (720 h), not the whole history.

health.unknownHint: Runs whose status code is none of the five canonical values. Counted here and never as successes — an unrecognised status is unknown, not fine.

strip.jobsAttentionHint: Jobs the contract calls bad: failed or completed-but-degraded. A run can report success while the jobs inside it did not.

statusMessage.previousJob: Open job {{id}} — the job this one waited on

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.noMessage: The runner recorded no message for this job.
diagnostics.captchaHint: A substring match on the page source: a captcha-like string was present in the HTML. It does not say a captcha was shown, blocked the session, or was solved — the runner records no solved-captcha signal at all.

liveness.hint: This view re-reads itself while a run is going, and pauses while the tab is in the background.

runAlarm.treatmentLostBody: {{name}} (Q-{{id}}) produced control-arm data while configured to be treated — this session cannot answer the experiment's question.
